'''''Prunus jamasakura''''', the '''Japanese mountain cherry''', is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family ''[[Rosaceae]]'' that is said to be [[Endemism|endemic]] to Japan.<ref name=POWO/> However, it is also said to be native to Korea, and to China.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=국립생물자원관 한반도의 생물다양성 (NIBR:Detail - ''Prunus jamasakura'') |url=https://species.nibr.go.kr/home/mainHome.do?cont_link=009&subMenu=009002&contCd=009002&pageMode=view&ktsn=120000061811 |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=species.nibr.go.kr}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
The species was first given a [[Binomial nomenclature|binomial]] by [[Philipp Franz von Siebold]] in 1830,<ref name="Siebold">{{cite journal |title=Synopsis Plantarum Oeconomicarum universi regni Japonici |language=la |author-first=Philipp Franz |author-last=von Siebold |author-link=Philipp Franz von Siebold |journal=Verhandelingen van het Bataviaasch Genootschap van Kunsten en Wetenschappen |year=1830 |volume=12 |page=68 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/41199001}}</ref><ref name="Lecto">{{cite journal |title=The Lectotypification of ''Prunus jamasakura'' and Allied Native Species of ''Cerasus'' sect. ''Sargentiella'' in Japan (Rosaceae—Prunoideae) |author-first1=Hideaki |author-last1=Ohba |author-link1=Hideaki Ohba |author-first2=Shinobu |author-last2=Akiyama |author-link2=Shinobu Akiyama |journal=Bulletin of the National Museum of Nature and Science. Series B (Botany) |publisher=[[National Museum of Nature and Science]] |volume=45 |issue=4 |pages=147–164 |date=22 November 2019}}</ref>{{rp|148}} the [[Botanical name|specific epithet]] relating to the [[Japanese language|Japanese]] [[common name]], {{nihongo||ヤマザクラ, 山桜|yama-zakura}},<ref name="IUCN"/> ''lit.'' the "mountain" or "wild cherry".<ref name="Lecto"/>{{rp|149}} While Siebold alludes to the uses to which the tree has traditionally been put—its wood in [[Woodblock printing in Japan|woodblock printing]], its bark in a range of crafts (''[[kabazaiku]]''), its fruit for consumption<ref name="Siebold"/><ref group="note">"Lignum exclusive in ''usum xylographorum'' versum, cortex pro diversis utensilibus ac fructus a pueris colliguntur."</ref>—there is no [[Species description|description]], [[Species diagnosis|diagnosis]], or reference to previous literature containing such, no illustration, and no mention of a [[Type (biology)|type specimen]],<ref name="Lecto"/>{{rp|148}} his ''Prunus jamasakura'' being a ''[[nomen nudum]]''<ref name="Lecto"/>{{rp|150}} or ''seminudum''.<ref name="Ohba">{{cite journal |title=Japanese Cherry Trees under the Genus Cerasus (Rosaceae) |author-first=Hideaki |author-last=Ohba |author-link=Hideaki Ohba |journal=[[Journal of Japanese Botany|The Journal of Japanese Botany]] |year=1992 |volume=67 |issue=5 |pages=276–281 |doi=10.51033/jjapbot.67_5_8728}}</ref>{{rp|278}}

[[Tomitaro Makino]] first [[Species description|described]] the [[taxon]] in 1908, as ''Prunus pseudocerasus'' var. ''jamasakura''.<ref name="Makino">{{cite journal |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/5435643 |title=Observations on the Flora of Japan. (Continued from p. 72.) |author-first=T. |author-last=Makino |author-link=Tomitaro Makino |journal=[[The Botanical Magazine (Tokyo)]] |year=1908 |volume=22 |issue=257 |pages=93–102 |doi=10.15281/jplantres1887.22.257_93}}</ref>{{rp|93}} Elevated to species rank (''Prunus jamasakura'') by [[Gen-ichi Koidzumi]] in 1911,<ref name="Koidzumi">{{cite journal |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/41812250 |title=Notes on Japanese Rosaceae. III. |author-first=G. |author-last=Koidzumi |author-link=Gen-ichi Koidzumi |journal=[[The Botanical Magazine (Tokyo)]] |year=1911 |volume=25 |issue=295 |pages=183–188 |doi=10.15281/jplantres1887.25.295_183}}</ref>{{rp|184}} in 1992 [[Hideaki Ohba]] moved the mountain cherry to the genus ''[[Prunus#Linnean classification|Cerasus]]'',<ref name="Ohba"/>{{rp|278}} a treatment still followed by a number of authorities.<ref name="Flora"/><ref name="Heibonsha"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://ylist.info/ylist_detail_display.php?pass=18494 |script-title=ja:植物和名ー学名インデックス |trans-title=YList |language=ja |author-first1=Koji |author-last1=Yonekura |author-first2=Tadashi |author-last2=Kajita |access-date=19 April 2024}}</ref> Ohba and [[Shinobu Akiyama]] suggest that Makino's var. ''jamasakura'' is a "superfluous name" and give the [[Author citation (botany)|citation]] ''Cerasus jamasakura'' (Siebold ex Koidz.) H. Ohba.<ref name="Lecto"/>{{rp|150}}

Two [[Variety (botany)|varieties]] are recognized:<ref name="POWO"/>
*''Prunus jamasakura'' var. ''chikusiensis'' ([[Gen-ichi Koidzumi|Koidz.]]) [[Jisaburo Ohwi|Ohwi]]<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/2365780 |script-title=ja:"日本植物誌"中に揭出せる植物の新学名及新組合せ |trans-title=New Scientific Names and New Combinations of Plants that can be found in "Flora of Japan" |language=ja |author-first=J. |author-last=Ohwi |author-link=Jisaburo Ohwi |journal=Bulletin of the National Science Museum |publisher=[[National Museum of Nature and Science|National Science Museum]] |year=1953 |volume=33 |pages=66–90 |doi=10.11501/2365780}}</ref>{{rp|76}} ([[Type locality (biology)|type locality]]: Tanegashima;<ref name="Tsukushi">{{cite journal |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/41605360 |title=Contributiones ad Floram Asiae Orientalis |language=la |author-first=Geniti |author-last=Koidzumi |author-link=Gen-ichi Koidzumi |journal=[[The Botanical Magazine (Tokyo)]] |year=1918 |volume=32 |issue=375 |pages=53–63 |doi=10.15281/jplantres1887.32.375_53}}</ref>{{rp|57}} {{nihongo||ツクシヤマザクラ|Tsukushi-yama-zakura}}<ref name="Ohba"/>{{rp|278}})
*''Prunus jamasakura'' var. ''jamasakura'' ([[Autonym (botany)|autonym]])

==Description==
''Prunus jamasakura'' is a [[deciduous]] tree that grows to a height of {{convert|20|–|25|m}}.<ref name="Flora">{{cite book |title=Flora of Japan. Volume IIb: Angiospermae, Dicotyledoneae, Archichlamydeae(b) |editor-first1=Kunio |editor-last1=Kunio |editor-first2=David Edward |editor-last2=Boufford |editor-first3=Hideaki |editor-last3=Ohba |editor-link3=Hideaki Ohba |year=2001 |publisher=Kodansha |place=Tokyo |isbn=4-06-154605-8 |pages=139–140}}</ref><ref name="Heibonsha">{{cite book |script-title=ja:日本の野生植物 第3巻 バラ科—センダン科 |trans-title=Wild Flowers of Japan. vol. 3: Rosaceae—Meliaceae |language=ja |editor-first1=Hiroyoshi |editor-last1=Ohashi |editor-link1=Hiroyoshi Ohashi |editor-first2=Yuichi |editor-last2=Kadota |editor-first3=Jin |editor-last3=Murata |editor-first4=Koji |editor-last4=Yonekura |year=2016 |publisher=[[Heibonsha]] |place=Tokyo |isbn=978-4-582-53533-4 |pages=67–68, pl. 48, 49}}</ref><ref name="Ohwi">{{cite book |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/30046456 |title=Flora of Japan (in English). A combined, much revised, and extended translation by the author of his 日本植物誌 FLORA OF JAPAN (1953) and 日本植物誌シダ篇 FLORA OF JAPAN—PTERIDOPHYTA (1957) |author-first=Jisaburo |author-last=Ohwi |author-link=Jisaburo Ohwi |publisher=[[Smithsonian Institution]] |place=[[Washington, D.C.]] |year=1965 |page=544}}</ref> Koidzumi's description is as follows: "a [[Glabrousness|glabrous]] tree, more rarely [[Pubescent (botany)|pubescent]]. [[Elliptic leaf|Elliptic leaves]] suddenly [[acuminate]], sharply [[:wiktionary:setaceous|setaceo]]-[[Serrated leaves|serrated]]. [[Petiole (botany)|Petioles]] arranged mostly towards the apex, with two [[Gland (botany)|glands]]. [[:wiktionary:coetaneous|Coetaneous]] flowers very rarely [[:wiktionary:sub-#Prefix|sub]][[:wiktionary:precocious|precocious]], [[corymb]]ose or [[Fascicle (botany)|fascicled]]. Glabrous [[Style (botany)|style]]."<ref name="Koidzumi"/>{{rp|185}}<ref group="note">"Arbor glaber rarius pubescens. Folia elliptica subito acuminata, argute setaceo-serrulata. Petioli plerumque versus apicem glandulis duobus instructi. Flores coaetanei rarissime subprecociores, corymbosi vel fasciculati. Stylus glaber."</ref> His description of the [[Kyushu|Tsukushi]] variety notes: "[[umbel]]s with shorter [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncles]], smaller [[bract]]s, and leaves' [[Serrate leaf|saw-teeth]] less [[Aristate (botany)|aristate]]".<ref name="Tsukushi"/>{{rp|57}}<ref group="note">"Umbellae pedunculis brevioribus, bracteis minoribus, foliorum serraturis brevius aristatis."</ref>

A study of the impact of feeding upon the fruit by [[Japanese black bear|black bears]] noted their preference for [[Ripening|ripe]] cherries (some 50–66 days after [[Flowering|blossoming]]) and found no [[significant difference]] in the percentage of seeds that [[Germination|germinated]] compared with the [[Scientific control|control]], suggesting their potential in [[Biological dispersal|dispersal]].<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://esj-journals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1007/s11284-007-0399-3 |title=Fruit phenology of ''Prunus jamasakura'' and the feeding habit of the Asiatic black bear as a seed disperser |author-first1=Shinsuke |author-last1=Koike  |author-first2=Shinsuke |author-last2=Kasai |author-first3=Koji |author-last3=Yamazaki |author-first4=Kengo |author-last4=Furubayashi |journal=Ecological Research |date=March 2008 |volume=23 |issue=2 |pages=385–392 |doi=10.1007/s11284-007-0399-3|bibcode=2008EcoR...23..385K |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Distribution==
The [[Endemism|endemic]]<ref name="Endemic">{{cite book |script-title=ja:日本の固有植物 |trans-title=Endemic Plants of Japan |language=ja |author1=Katō, M. |author-link=:ja:加藤雅啓 |author2=Ebihara, A. |author-link2=:ja:海老原淳 |date=March 2011 |publisher=[[Tokai University Press]] |isbn=978-4-486-01897-1 |pages=77, 316}}</ref> species occurs in the low mountains and [[Secondary forest|secondary forests]] of Japan, from the [[Kantō region]] of [[Honshu|Honshū]] to [[Shikoku]] and [[Kyushu|Kyūshū]].<ref name="IUCN"/><ref name="Ohwi"/> The Tsukushi variety is found on the islands surrounding Kyūshū, including [[Tsushima Island|Tsushima]], [[Tanegashima]], and the [[Tokara Islands]].<ref name="POWO"/><ref name="Ohwi"/>

==Conservation status==
''Prunus jamasakura'' is classed as [[Least-concern species|Least Concern]] on the [[International Union for Conservation of Nature|IUCN]] [[IUCN Red List|Red List]], although the 2021 assessment notes a decline in the area and quality of its habitat.<ref name="IUCN">{{cite iucn |author=Oldfield, S. |year=2021 |title=''Prunus jamasakura''  |article-number=e.T173917565A173917817 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2021-1.RLTS.T173917565A173917817.en}}</ref>

==Cultural significance==
The mountain cherry, even if its historic [[Circumscription (taxonomy)|circumscription]] hasn't always conformed with current [[Taxonomy (biology)|taxonomic]] understanding and [[molecular phylogenetics]], has inspired [[Japanese poetry|Japanese poets]] since the days of the ''[[Man'yōshū]]'' and long been the object of the practices of appreciation known as ''[[hanami]]''.<ref>{{cite book |script-title=ja:万葉植物事典「万葉植物を読む」|trans-title=Encyclopaedia of Man'yō Plants |language=ja |author-first1=Yamada |author-last1=Takuzō |author-link1=:ja:山田卓三 |author-first2=Shintarõ |author-last2=Nakajima |year=1995 |publisher=[[:ja:北隆館|Hokuryukan]] |isbn=4-8326-0374-4 |pages=263–269}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |script-title=ja:桜 |trans-title=Sakura |language=ja |author-first=Toshio |author-last=Katsuki |year=2015 |publisher=[[Iwanami Shoten]] |isbn=978-4-00-431534-6 |pages=86-95, 106, 166-168}}</ref><!--citation from [[Hanami]]--> Records of its full blossoming and of viewing parties in [[Edo period]] diaries and chronicles are such that they have been drawn on more recently for the reconstruction of historic temperatures.<ref name="Aono">{{cite journal |title=Cherry blossom phenological data since the seventeenth century for Edo (Tokyo), Japan, and their application to estimation of March temperatures |author-first=Yasuyuki |author-last=Aono |journal=[[International Journal of Biometeorology]] |year=2014 |volume=59 |issue=4 |pages=427–435 |doi=10.1007/s00484-014-0854-0 |pmid=24899397}}</ref>

== Uses ==
In [[South Korea]] this cherry is used an ornamental, and the wood is used for building materials, furniture, musical instruments, and carving. The fruit is edible and the bark is used medicinally.<ref name=":0" />
